question:
Match the refrigerant control expansion valves with their correct functions.

 
 

 Refrigerant controls
 Functions
 
 

 A. Suction-line regulators
 P. Limit the flow of gas to the compressor to prevent s loads
 
 

 B. Check valves
 Q. Interrupt the flow on demand from any one of sev temperature or pressure-sensing devices
 
 

 C. Solenoid valves
 R. Prevent the flow of gas from the condenser
 
 

 D. Hold back valves
 S. Control the flow of refrigerant gas from the evaporator
solution:
__**Explanation:**__

**Refrigerant Control Expansion Valves:**

 
• Refrigerant control expansion valves are critical components in refrigeration and air conditioning systems. They regulate the flow of refrigerant to maintain optimal system performance, ensure efficiency, and prevent potential damage to the compressor. Different types of control valves serve specific purposes in the refrigeration cycle.

**Suction-line regulators:**

 
• Suction-line regulators are designed to control the suction pressure in the refrigeration system. By limiting the flow of refrigerant gas to the compressor, these regulators prevent the compressor from being overloaded. This function ensures the efficient operation of the compressor and protects it from potential damage due to excessive loads.

**Check valves:**

 
• Check valves are one-way valves that allow fluid or gas to flow in only one direction. In refrigeration systems, check valves prevent the backflow of refrigerant gas from the condenser. This ensures the proper flow of refrigerant through the system and prevents issues such as pressure imbalances or reverse flow, which could lead to system inefficiency or damage.

**Solenoid valves:**

 
• Solenoid valves are electrically operated valves used to control the flow of refrigerant. These valves can open or close in response to signals from temperature or pressure-sensing devices. This allows for precise control of the refrigerant flow based on system demands, ensuring optimal performance and energy efficiency.

**Hold back valves:**

 
• Hold back valves are used to regulate the flow of refrigerant gas exiting the evaporator. By controlling this flow, these valves maintain the desired pressure in the evaporator, ensuring efficient heat exchange and preventing issues such as liquid refrigerant reaching the compressor.
 
• **A. Suction-line regulators → P. Limit the flow of gas to the compressor to prevent overloads**
 
• **B. Check valves → R. Prevent the flow of gas from the condenser**
 
• **C. Solenoid valves → Q. Interrupt the flow on demand from any one of several temperature or pressure-sensing devices**
 
• **D. Hold back valves → S. Control the flow of refrigerant gas from the evaporator**

The correct option is therefore:

**Option 4: A-P, B-R, C-Q, D-S**
